meta.title: Driving through intersections
meta.summary: You will learn to quickly work out who goes through an intersection first: at traffic lights, on a main or minor road, on roads of equal status, and on a roundabout.

p: An intersection is a place where roads cross, join or branch at the same level. Its boundaries are imaginary lines connecting the starting points of the carriageway corner curves ⟦20⟧.

Under the Rules, “give way” means not starting, not resuming and not continuing to move, and not making a manoeuvre, if this would force a road user with priority to change direction or speed ⟦21⟧. In other words, it is not enough just to “squeeze through in time”: the other driver must not have to brake or swerve because of you.
At any intersection, first answer one question: who controls the order of priority here? The answer determines which rules apply.
Check from top to bottom. As soon as you find the answer, stop there.
list: Traffic controller. Their signals are obeyed even if they contradict the traffic lights, signs or road markings ⟦22⟧. Arms extended to the sides or lowered: from either side, trackless vehicles may go straight ahead or right (a tram, only straight ahead); facing the chest or the back, you must stop. Right arm extended forward: from the left side, trackless vehicles may go in any direction (a tram, only left); facing the chest, only right; facing the right side or the back, you must stop. Arm raised up: everyone stops, except those who cannot stop without emergency braking ⟦23⟧.
Traffic lights. If they are working normally, the intersection is controlled ⟦24⟧.
Priority signs. They decide the order when the traffic lights are flashing amber, switched off, or absent altogether ⟦25⟧.
Road surface. If there are no signs, a paved road (asphalt, concrete, stone) has priority over a dirt road ⟦26⟧.
None of this applies: it is an intersection of roads of equal status, and the “priority to the right” rule applies ⟦27⟧.
lesson.tip: A flashing amber signal is not “almost red”; it is a sign that the intersection has become uncontrolled. Look for priority signs.

p: These three rules apply everywhere: with or without traffic lights.
list: Turning right or left: give way to pedestrians crossing the road you are turning into, and to cyclists on a cycle track. Also give way to buses and other public transport in a lane marked with sign 5.9 ⟦28⟧. From 2026, you may not enter such a lane even across a broken line ⟦29⟧, so you turn from the adjacent lane after giving way to route vehicles.
A traffic jam ahead? Do not enter the intersection if you would have to stop on it and block vehicles moving across your path. Even if the light is green ⟦30⟧.

Do not pass vehicles at the intersection that are travelling in the same direction and blocking your view. If a vehicle has stopped in the next lane at or before the intersection, only continue once you have made sure it is safe: it may be giving way to a pedestrian you cannot see ⟦31⟧.

lesson.h: Traffic lights: turning left and making a U-turn
p: A green signal permits several flows of traffic to move at once, including oncoming traffic. So when turning left or making a U-turn on green, you give way to oncoming vehicles that are going straight ahead or turning right ⟦32⟧.

This also applies to oncoming vehicles that enter the intersection on an amber signal or while the traffic controller's arm is raised, because they cannot stop without emergency braking (para. 37; for amber, only if it was not preceded by a flashing green), and to those whom the traffic controller has allowed to move ⟦33⟧. Trams follow the same rule among themselves ⟦34⟧.

If an oncoming vehicle is also turning left, vehicles pass each other on their right-hand sides: each one turns in front of the oncoming vehicle, keeping the centre of the intersection on its right, and both move at the same time. The exception is intersections with an unusual layout where this manoeuvre is not possible ⟦35⟧.
lesson.tip: Turning left on green: always look for oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or turning right. You give way to them.

lesson.h: Green comes on: look around first
list: The light is red, or the traffic controller prohibits movement: stop before the stop line or sign 5.33, and if there is neither, before the intersecting carriageway, without blocking pedestrians ⟦36⟧.
Green does not give you the right to move off straight away. Give way to vehicles still finishing their way through the intersection, and to pedestrians who have not finished crossing ⟦37⟧.

If you crossed the stop line (sign 5.33) on green, continue in your intended direction even if the signal has changed by the time you exit. Exception: if the traffic lights ahead of you have their own stop lines or sign 5.33, obey the signals of each traffic light ⟦38⟧.
Are you in a turning lane with the filter arrow lit, and other vehicles are coming up behind you in the same lane? Keep moving on the arrow if stopping would block the vehicles behind you ⟦39⟧.

lesson.h: The filter arrow and the tram
p: A green filter arrow in the additional section can be lit at the same time as a red or amber signal. You may drive on it, but this permission is “second class”: you give way to everyone moving from other directions ⟦40⟧.

If the traffic lights permit a tram and other vehicles to move at the same time, the tram has priority, whichever way it is going. But if the tram is moving on an arrow lit together with a red or amber signal, it is the tram that gives way to everyone else ⟦41⟧.

A main road is marked with signs 2.1, 2.3.1-2.3.3 or 5.1. If there are no signs, a paved road counts as the main road in relation to a dirt road. A short stretch of asphalt on a minor road right before the intersection does not make it equal to the road it crosses ⟦42⟧.

If you are driving on a minor road, give way to everyone approaching on the main road, whichever way they are going: straight ahead, right, left or making a U-turn ⟦43⟧. A minor road is usually marked with sign 2.4 “Give way” or 2.5 “No passing without stopping”. At sign 2.5 you must stop before the stop line, and if there is none, before the edge of the intersecting carriageway.
list: If the main road has a central reservation and you are making a U-turn at the intersection, before completing the U-turn make sure that vehicles from the minor road are actually giving way to you ⟦44⟧.
Everyone on the minor road gives way: a tram, and a vehicle with an amber beacon too. Such a beacon does not exempt a driver from the requirements of signs 2.4 and 2.5 ⟦45⟧.
You must give way to those whose path you cross or whose lane you are entering. When turning right, you do not get in the way of a vehicle travelling in the far lane in the other direction ⟦46⟧.
lesson.tip: For a driver on the minor road, it does not matter where a vehicle on the main road is going: if its path crosses yours, you wait, even if it is making a U-turn.

lesson.h: When the main road changes direction
p: The direction of the main road is shown by plate 7.13 “Direction of the priority road” under the priority sign. If the main road changes direction at the intersection, drivers on the main road follow the rules for roads of equal status among themselves: priority to the right, and give way to oncoming vehicles when turning left. Drivers on the minor roads follow the same rule among themselves ⟦47⟧.

At the same time, the minor road still gives way to the main road. A driver approaching on the main road goes before one approaching on a minor road, even if the driver on the main road is turning off it ⟦48⟧.
lesson.tip: First split the vehicles into two groups: those on the main road and those on the minor road. Within each group, the priority-to-the-right rule applies.

lesson.h: Roads of equal status: priority to the right
list: Give way to a vehicle approaching from the right ⟦49⟧.
Turning left or making a U-turn: give way to oncoming vehicles that are going straight ahead or turning right ⟦50⟧.
At an intersection of roads of equal status, a tram has priority over other vehicles, whichever way it is coming from. Trams follow the priority-to-the-right rule among themselves ⟦51⟧.
At night, or in mud or snow, you cannot see whether there is a paved surface under your wheels, and there are no priority signs? Treat yourself as being on a minor road ⟦52⟧.

p: Everyone gives way to a vehicle with a flashing blue or red beacon and a special audible signal switched on, even if you have a green light or are on the main road ⟦53⟧. Its driver may depart from traffic light signals, signs and the rules for driving through intersections (but not from the traffic controller's signals), and only uses this priority after making sure that other road users are giving way ⟦54⟧.

Both signals matter. If only the beacon is on and the special audible signal is off, there is no priority, and such a vehicle is given way to under the general rules. An amber or yellow beacon gives no priority at all ⟦55⟧.
lesson.tip: First give way to the emergency vehicle, then work out the rest as usual: the order of priority for everyone else does not change.

p: A roundabout is marked with sign 4.3 “Roundabout”: you may only drive round it in the direction of the arrows, that is, anticlockwise (sign 4.3).

Important: the current Rules of Kazakhstan have no separate provision giving priority to those already on the roundabout. A roundabout is an intersection, and the order of priority on it is set by priority signs, or, if there are none, by the general rules.
list: Is there a priority sign before the entry, most often 2.4 “Give way”? Then the vehicle entering gives way to those already on the roundabout.

No priority signs? It is an intersection of roads of equal status. The vehicle entering approaches those on the roundabout from the right, so vehicles on the roundabout give way to vehicles entering ⟦56⟧.
When entering a roundabout, you do not have to take up the extreme position in advance ⟦57⟧.
Leaving a roundabout is a right turn, and there is no exception for it: take up the far right position in advance ⟦58⟧.
lesson.tip: At a roundabout, first look for sign 2.4 at the entry. If it is there, the vehicle entering gives way. If not, it is priority to the right, and the vehicle on the roundabout gives way.

lesson.h: Yards, field tracks and turning into a yard
p: Not every joining road is an intersection. Exits from adjacent areas (yards, car parks, filling stations) and places where field and forest tracks join a road do not count as intersections ⟦59⟧, so priority to the right does not apply there.
list: Coming out of a yard: give way to all road users ⟦60⟧.
Entering a road from a minor road, for example a field dirt track: give way to vehicles and pedestrians on that road ⟦61⟧.
Turning off the road into a yard: give way to those whose path you cross, including pedestrians on the pavement. When turning left outside an intersection, give way to oncoming vehicles ⟦62⟧.

lesson.h: Where you may turn: signs, markings and lanes
list: Signs 4.1.1-4.1.6 permit only the directions shown, at the intersection before which they are placed. A sign permitting a left turn also permits a U-turn.
Signs 3.18.1 and 3.18.2 prohibit a right or left turn, and sign 3.19 prohibits only a U-turn.
Arrows of marking 1.18 show where you may go from that lane. A left arrow in the far left lane also permits a U-turn.
Turn into the matching lane: from the far right lane into the far right lane, from the far left lane into the far left lane ⟦63⟧.
You may enter a roundabout from a lane other than the far right one, but you must leave it from the far right lane ⟦64⟧.
A cyclist must not turn left or make a U-turn on roads with a tram or where there is more than one lane in their direction ⟦65⟧.

lesson.h: How to work out the order of priority
list: 1. An emergency vehicle with a beacon and a special audible signal goes first.
2. Who controls the intersection: traffic controller, traffic lights, signs, road surface. If it is traffic lights, first those finishing their way through, then by the signals.
3. At an intersection of unequal roads, split the vehicles into main road and minor road. The minor road waits for everyone on the main road whose path it crosses.
4. Within each group: a tram before trackless vehicles, then priority to the right, and a vehicle turning left or making a U-turn gives way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or turning right.
5. Vehicles whose paths do not cross move at the same time. A vehicle that must give way to someone waits, even if that other vehicle is itself giving way to someone.
lesson.tip: Check every pair of vehicles: whether their paths cross, and which of the two must give way. This solves any problem, even one with four vehicles.

keyFacts: Flashing amber or switched-off traffic lights: the intersection is uncontrolled, and priority signs apply ⟦1⟧.
The traffic controller's signals are obeyed even if they contradict the traffic lights, signs and road markings ⟦2⟧.
When turning right or left, give way to pedestrians on the road you are turning into, cyclists on a cycle track, and route vehicles in a lane marked with sign 5.9 ⟦3⟧.
You must not enter an intersection in a traffic jam if you would have to stop and block vehicles moving across your path ⟦4⟧.

Turning left or making a U-turn on green: give way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or right, including those entering on amber ⟦5⟧. Oncoming vehicles turning left pass each other on their right-hand sides ⟦6⟧.
After green comes on, give way to vehicles finishing their way through and to pedestrians who have not finished crossing ⟦7⟧.

Driving on an arrow lit together with a red or amber signal: give way to everyone from other directions. When one signal permits both a tram and other vehicles to move, the tram has priority regardless of direction ⟦8⟧.
A minor road gives way to the main road regardless of the direction a vehicle on the main road is going, including a U-turn ⟦9⟧.
If the main road changes direction, drivers on the main road follow the rules for roads of equal status among themselves, and so do drivers on the minor roads ⟦10⟧.
Roads of equal status: priority to the right; when turning left or making a U-turn, give way to oncoming vehicles; a tram has priority over trackless vehicles regardless of direction ⟦11⟧.
No priority signs and you cannot see the road surface: treat yourself as being on a minor road ⟦12⟧.
Everyone gives way to an emergency vehicle with a beacon and a special audible signal; an amber beacon gives no priority ⟦13⟧.
mistakes: “I am turning left on green, so I have priority.” No: green is also lit for oncoming traffic. Give way to those coming towards you and going straight ahead or turning right ⟦14⟧.
Moving off as soon as green comes on. First give way to those finishing their way through, and to pedestrians still on the crossing ⟦15⟧.

Treating an exit from a yard or a field track as an intersection where priority to the right applies. This is not an intersection: the driver coming out gives way to everyone travelling along the road ⟦16⟧.

Thinking that on a roundabout, those already on the roundabout always have priority. Kazakhstan's Rules have no such rule: priority signs decide, and without them, whoever has a vehicle on their right gives way, which is the one already on the roundabout ⟦17⟧.
Thinking that when the main road changes direction, anyone on the main road goes first. Among themselves, drivers on the main road follow the priority-to-the-right rule ⟦18⟧.
Entering an intersection on green when there is a traffic jam right beyond it. If you get stuck in the middle of the intersection, you have broken the ban on entering during a traffic jam ⟦19⟧.

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection. The traffic lights are flashing amber. How do you work out the order of priority?
options: As with an ordinary amber: you must stop at the stop line
The intersection is closed; you must wait for green to come on
By the priority signs, as at an uncontrolled intersection
Vehicles going straight ahead have priority, and everyone else gives way
questions.explain: With a flashing amber signal, non-working traffic lights, or no traffic controller, the intersection counts as uncontrolled. The order of priority is set by the priority signs and the rules for driving through uncontrolled intersections.

questions.q: At an intersection, the traffic lights are working and a traffic controller is also present. The traffic lights show red for you, but the traffic controller's signal allows you to go. What should you do?
options: Wait for green: the traffic lights take precedence over the traffic controller
Go: the traffic controller's signals are obeyed
Wait until the traffic controller switches off the traffic lights
questions.explain: Drivers obey the traffic controller's signals and instructions, even if they contradict the traffic light signals or the requirements of signs or road markings.

questions.q: You are turning right on a green signal. Pedestrians are crossing, on a pedestrian crossing, the road you are turning into. What must you do?
options: Go first: you also have a green signal
Sound your horn so the pedestrians stop
Go ahead of the pedestrians if they have only just stepped onto the crossing
Give way to the pedestrians and only then complete the turn
questions.explain: When turning right or left, a driver gives way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway of the road they are turning into. A pedestrian must not have to change speed or direction because of you.

questions.q: At a controlled intersection, you are turning left on a green signal. A car is coming towards you going straight ahead, and behind it a bus is turning right. What should you do?
options: Give way to both oncoming vehicles, then turn left
Turn first: you entered the intersection earlier
Give way only to the car: the bus turning right gives way to you
Give way only to the bus, because it is bigger
questions.explain: When turning left or making a U-turn on a permitting signal, a driver gives way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or turning right. It does not matter who entered the intersection first.

questions.q: The light is green. There is a traffic jam right beyond the intersection: if you enter, you will stop in the middle of the intersection and block vehicles moving across your path. What should you do?
options: Do not enter until there is room beyond the intersection
Enter: as long as the light is green, you have the right to go
Enter and wait on the intersection with your hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: You must not enter an intersection if a traffic jam has formed that would force you to stop and create an obstruction for traffic moving across your path. A green signal does not cancel this ban.

questions.q: You are the first vehicle at the stop line. Green comes on. At that moment, a vehicle is finishing crossing the intersection across your path, and a pedestrian who has not finished crossing is still on the crossing ahead. What should you do?
options: Move off straight away: green gives you priority
Give way to the vehicle and the pedestrian, then move off
Give way only to the pedestrian: the vehicle should have stopped
Give way only to the vehicle: the pedestrian must wait
questions.explain: When a permitting signal comes on, a driver gives way to vehicles finishing their way through the intersection and to pedestrians who have not finished crossing.

questions.q: You crossed the stop line on green to turn left, and stopped in the centre of the intersection, giving way to the oncoming flow of traffic. While you were waiting, red came on. There are no other traffic lights with a stop line on your path. What should you do?
options: Stay where you are until the next green
Reverse back behind the stop line
Turn right instead of left, so as not to get in anyone's way
Complete the left turn and clear the intersection
questions.explain: A driver who has crossed the stop line on a permitting signal exits in the intended direction regardless of the signals at the exit ⟦66⟧. Drivers for whom green comes on must give way to you as a vehicle finishing its way through ⟦67⟧.

questions.q: You are turning right on a green filter arrow in the additional section. The main signal for you is red. On the left, along the road you are crossing, a vehicle is moving on its own green. Who goes first?
options: You: the green arrow gives you priority
You: the vehicle is approaching from the left, so it is the one facing an obstacle
The vehicle on the left: on such an arrow, you give way to everyone
questions.explain: If you are driving on an arrow lit in the additional section at the same time as a red or amber signal, you give way to vehicles from all other directions.

questions.q: At a controlled intersection, the green signal permits you and an oncoming tram to move at the same time. You are going straight ahead, and the tram is turning left, crossing your path. Who goes first?
options: You: a vehicle turning left gives way to oncoming vehicles
The tram, even though it is turning left
You: trackless vehicles always have priority over a tram
questions.explain: If the signals permit a tram and trackless vehicles to move at the same time, the tram has priority regardless of its direction of travel. Trams apply the “turning left gives way to oncoming vehicles” rule only among themselves.

questions.q: You are stopped on a minor road at sign 2.4 “Give way” and want to turn left. A vehicle with its left indicator on is approaching along the main road from the left: it is about to make a U-turn at this intersection. What should you do?
options: Give way to it, then turn
Turn first: a driver making a U-turn must give way to everyone
Turn first, if it has not yet started the U-turn
questions.explain: A driver on a minor road gives way to vehicles approaching on the main road regardless of the direction they will go next, including those making a U-turn.

questions.q: You are driving on the main road. At the intersection, the main road turns left (as shown by plate 7.13), and you keep going straight ahead, that is, you turn off the main road. On the right, a vehicle is approaching the intersection along a minor road, also going straight ahead. Who goes first?
options: The vehicle on the right: you are turning off the main road and losing priority
The vehicle on the right: priority to the right applies
You, because you are approaching on the main road
questions.explain: A driver on a minor road gives way to everyone approaching on the main road, regardless of the direction they will go next. When the main road changes direction, the priority-to-the-right rule applies only among drivers on the main road, and separately among drivers on minor roads.

questions.q: You are driving on the main road, which turns right at the intersection (plate 7.13). You keep going straight ahead. On the right, along the same main road, a vehicle is approaching the intersection going straight ahead, across your path. Who goes first?
options: You: you are going straight ahead, so you have priority
You: it is turning off the main road and must give way to you
The vehicle on the right: priority to the right applies between you
questions.explain: When the main road changes direction at the intersection, drivers on it follow the rules for roads of equal status among themselves. So you give way to the vehicle approaching from the right ⟦68⟧.

questions.q: An intersection of roads of equal status, with no signs or traffic lights. You are going straight ahead. A vehicle is approaching the intersection from the right, also going straight ahead. Who goes first?
options: You: you are closer to the centre of the intersection
questions.explain: At an intersection of roads of equal status, the driver of a trackless vehicle gives way to vehicles approaching from the right.

questions.q: An intersection of roads of equal status. You are turning left. A vehicle is coming towards you going straight ahead, and there is no one on the right or left. What should you do?
options: Give way to the oncoming vehicle and turn after it
Turn first: the oncoming vehicle is not approaching from the right, so there is no obstacle
questions.explain: When turning left or making a U-turn at an intersection of equal status, a driver gives way to vehicles moving from the opposite direction, going straight ahead or turning right.

questions.q: An intersection of roads of equal status. You are going straight ahead. A tram is approaching the intersection from the left, also going straight ahead. Who goes first?
options: You: the tram is approaching from the left, so it must give way
You, if the tram is moving slowly
The tram, even though it is approaching from the left
questions.explain: At an intersection of roads of equal status, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles regardless of its direction of travel. The priority-to-the-right rule does not help here.

questions.q: It is night, and it is snowing. You are approaching an intersection and cannot tell whether your road has an asphalt surface. There are no priority signs. What should you assume?
options: That you are on the main road until you see a sign
That the main road is the one more vehicles are travelling on
That you are on a minor road
questions.explain: If it is impossible to tell whether there is a paved surface (darkness, mud, snow) and there are no priority signs, a driver assumes they are on a minor road.

questions.q: You are driving round a roundabout intersection (sign 4.3). There are no priority signs at this intersection, and all the roads are paved. A vehicle is entering the roundabout on your right, and its path crosses yours. Who gives way?
options: You: the vehicle entering is approaching you from the right
The vehicle entering: whoever is already on the roundabout always has priority
The vehicle entering, if you have your indicator on
questions.explain: Kazakhstan's Rules have no separate rule giving priority to those already on a roundabout. If there are no priority signs, a roundabout is treated as an intersection of roads of equal status, and drivers give way to whoever is on their right. For a driver already on the roundabout, the vehicle entering is on the right.

questions.q: Signs 4.3 “Roundabout” and 2.4 “Give way” are placed before the entry to a roundabout intersection. A vehicle is approaching you on the roundabout from the left. What should you do?
options: Enter first: it is approaching from the left
Enter first, if you have already switched on your indicator
Give way to the vehicle on the roundabout, then enter
questions.explain: Sign 2.4 requires giving way to vehicles moving along the road being crossed. Here, the road being crossed is the roundabout, so a vehicle entering gives way to those already on it.

questions.q: There are no priority signs or traffic lights. Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: There are no signs or traffic lights, so this is an intersection of roads of equal status. The truck is approaching from the right, so you give way to it. The green car on the left is turning right, and its path does not cross yours.

questions.q: Who must the driver of the white truck give way to?
questions.explain: The intersection is one of equal status. The blue car is approaching you from the left, so it is the one giving way to you ⟦69⟧. The green car is turning right, away from you, so your paths do not cross.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who do you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: The oncoming bus is going straight ahead, so when turning left you must give way to it ⟦70⟧. The motorcycle on the left is turning right and does not cross your path. It will actually go first: for the bus, the motorcycle is approaching from the right ⟦71⟧.

questions.q: There are no signs. In what order will the vehicles go through the intersection?
questions.explain: The intersection is one of equal status: the blue car is on the white car's right, so the white car waits for it even though it is going straight ahead ⟦72⟧. The truck is turning left and gives way to the oncoming white car ⟦73⟧. Result: blue, white, truck.

questions.q: You want to make a U-turn at this intersection. Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: When making a U-turn at an intersection of equal status, you give way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or turning right ⟦74⟧, that is, the blue car. The taxi on the right is turning right and leaving the intersection without crossing your path.

questions.q: Who must the driver of the blue car give way to?
questions.explain: The white car is making a U-turn and must give way to you as an oncoming vehicle going straight ahead ⟦75⟧. The taxi is on your left and is turning right, so your paths do not cross. You do not need to give way to anyone.

questions.q: There are no signs or traffic lights. In what order will all the vehicles go through the intersection?
questions.explain: For the blue car, the green car is on the right and is turning into the same road the blue car is taking, so the blue car gives way to it; and for the truck, the blue car is on the right ⟦76⟧. You are turning left and give way both to the oncoming blue car ⟦77⟧ and to the truck on your right ⟦78⟧. So: green, blue, truck, you.

questions.q: There are no signs, and both roads are paved. Who do you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: There are no priority signs and the surface is the same on both roads, so the intersection is one of equal status, even though one of the roads runs straight through. The truck is approaching from the right, so you give way to it. For the green car, you yourself are on the right, so it gives way to you ⟦79⟧.

questions.q: There are no signs, and both roads are paved. Who must the driver of the green car give way to?
questions.explain: The blue car is coming out of a joining road on your right. There are no signs, so priority to the right applies, and you must give way to it ⟦80⟧. You and the truck are travelling straight towards each other, so your paths do not cross.

questions.q: There are no signs. In what order will the taxi, the blue car and the motorcycle go through the intersection?
questions.explain: The taxi is turning left: it gives way both to the oncoming blue car ⟦81⟧ and to the motorcycle, which is on its right ⟦82⟧. The motorcycle gives way to the blue car, because the blue car is on its right. So: blue, motorcycle, taxi.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must the driver of the truck give way to?
options: The orange car and the green car
The orange car and the blue car
questions.explain: The orange car on the right is turning right into the same road you are taking, so you must give way to it ⟦83⟧. The green car is turning left and gives way to you, because you are on its right. You and the blue car are travelling straight towards each other and do not cross paths.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must the driver of the green car give way to?
options: The truck and the orange car
The truck, the orange car and the blue car
questions.explain: You are turning left, and the oncoming orange car is turning right into the same road, so you must give way to it ⟦84⟧. The truck is approaching from the right, so you give way to it too ⟦85⟧. For the blue car, you yourself are on the right, so it waits for you.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must you give way to when turning right?
questions.explain: The white car is approaching from the left, so it gives way to you ⟦86⟧. The black car is coming towards you and turning left into the same road as you, so it gives way to you as an oncoming vehicle turning right ⟦87⟧.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must the driver of the black car give way to?
questions.explain: You are turning left into the same road that the motorcycle and the white car are taking. The motorcycle is an oncoming vehicle turning right, and you give way to it when turning left ⟦88⟧. The white car is approaching from the right ⟦89⟧, so you must give way to both.

questions.q: There are no signs. In what order will the bus, the blue car and the red car go through the intersection?
questions.explain: The bus is turning left and gives way to the blue car, which is on its right ⟦90⟧. For the red car, the bus is on the right, so the red car waits for the bus, even though its path does not cross the blue car's. Result: blue, bus, red.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must you give way to?
options: The cyclist and the blue car
questions.explain: A cyclist is also a driver, and at an intersection of equal status, priority to the right applies to them too ⟦91⟧. The cyclist is on your right, so you give way to them. The blue car is coming towards you going straight ahead and does not cross your path, but it will go first: for the cyclist, it is on the right.

questions.q: There are no signs. The white car is making a U-turn. In what order will the vehicles go through the intersection?
questions.explain: The white car is making a U-turn: it gives way to the oncoming green car ⟦92⟧ and to the truck on its right ⟦93⟧. The truck gives way to the green car, because the green car is on its right. Result: green, truck, white.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who do you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: When turning left, you give way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or turning right ⟦94⟧. The oncoming blue car is turning right into the same road you are turning into, so you must give way to it. The green car on the left is turning right and driving away without crossing your path.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: The intersection is one of equal status. The green car is approaching from the left, so it is the one giving way to you ⟦95⟧. The oncoming blue car is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must the driver of the green car give way to?
questions.explain: The white car is approaching you from the right, and there are no priority signs, so you must give way to it ⟦96⟧. The blue car is turning right and driving away in the lane that is oncoming for you, so your paths do not cross.

questions.q: Who must you give way to when turning right?
questions.explain: You are on a minor road (sign 2.4) and give way to vehicles on the main road if they would otherwise have to brake because of you ⟦97⟧. The blue car on the left is travelling in the lane you are turning into, so you must give way to it. The green car is travelling in the far lane in the other direction, so it does not get in the way of your turn.

questions.q: Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: You are on the main road (sign 2.1). The white car, on the minor road (sign 2.4), must give way to you, even though it is turning into your lane ⟦98⟧. The green car is coming towards you going straight ahead and does not cross your path.

questions.q: Who must you give way to?
options: The truck and the blue car
questions.explain: You are on the minor road, and the truck, coming from the main road, is turning left and crossing your path, so you give way to it ⟦99⟧. The blue car, from the main road, is turning right and does not cross your path. The taxi is coming towards you along the same minor road going straight ahead, so your paths do not cross either.

questions.q: In what order will the truck, the red car and the blue car go through the intersection?
questions.explain: The truck is on the main road, so it goes first, even though it is turning left ⟦100⟧. The red car and the blue car are on the minor road: they stop at sign 2.5, and among themselves they follow the rules for a road of equal status. The blue car is turning left and gives way to the oncoming red car ⟦101⟧.

questions.q: Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: You are driving on the main road (sign 2.1), so priority to the right does not apply here: the bus, on the minor road (sign 2.4), gives way to you ⟦102⟧. The green car is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: Who must the driver of the bus give way to?
questions.explain: You are on the minor road (sign 2.4) and give way to the black car, which is on the main road and crosses your path ⟦103⟧. The green car is coming towards you and turning right, so your paths do not cross.

questions.q: Who do you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: You are on the minor road and give way to those on the main road whose path crosses yours ⟦104⟧. The truck on the right is going straight ahead across your path, so you must give way to it. The blue car on the left is turning right into your road, and it does not cross your turn.

questions.q: Who must the driver of the truck give way to?
questions.explain: You are driving on the main road. The orange car, on the minor road, gives way to you wherever you are going ⟦105⟧. The oncoming blue car is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: In what order will all four vehicles go through the intersection?
questions.explain: First, those on the main road: the blue car is going straight ahead, and the truck is turning left and gives way to the oncoming blue car ⟦106⟧. Then the minor road ⟦107⟧: the white car is going straight ahead, and the green car is turning left and gives way to the oncoming white car ⟦108⟧.

questions.q: There is sign 2.5 ahead of you. Who do you give way to after the compulsory stop?
questions.explain: Sign 2.5 requires you to stop at the edge of the intersecting carriageway, and then give way to vehicles on the main road. The blue car on the right is going straight ahead and crosses your path, so you give way to it. The green car is turning right into your road and does not cross your path.

questions.q: In what order will the motorcycle, the blue car and the bus go through the intersection?
questions.explain: Sign 2.3.2 for the blue car and sign 2.1 for the bus show that they are on the main road, while the motorcycle, at sign 2.4, is on the minor road. The bus is turning left and gives way to the oncoming blue car ⟦109⟧. The motorcycle gives way to the bus, which crosses its path, so it goes last ⟦110⟧.

questions.q: Who must you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: You are on the main road, so the green car, on the minor road, gives way to you ⟦111⟧. The oncoming truck is also on the main road, and among yourselves you follow the rules for a road of equal status: when turning left, you give way to an oncoming vehicle going straight ahead ⟦112⟧.

questions.q: Who do you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: You and the truck are both on the main road, and the black car is on the minor road (sign 2.4). When turning left, you give way to the oncoming truck, which is going straight ahead ⟦113⟧. The black car is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: Who must the driver of the black car give way to?
questions.explain: You are on the minor road and turning right, into the lane the truck from the main road is travelling in. You must give way to it ⟦114⟧. The blue car, from the main road, is turning left into your road, but in the lane that is oncoming for you, so your paths do not cross.

questions.q: The red car is making a U-turn. In what order will the vehicles go through the intersection?
options: Red, then blue, then green and the bus at the same time
Green and the bus at the same time, then blue, then red
Blue, then green and the bus at the same time, then red
Blue, then red, then green and the bus at the same time
questions.explain: The red car and the blue car are on the main road: the red car is making a U-turn and gives way to the oncoming blue car ⟦115⟧. The green car and the bus, on the minor road (sign 2.5), stop and wait for both vehicles from the main road to go through ⟦116⟧. Their paths do not cross each other, so they go at the same time.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: You are coming out of a dirt road onto a paved one. Without signs, a paved road counts as the main road in relation to a dirt road ⟦117⟧, so you give way to the truck, which crosses your path ⟦118⟧. The blue car is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: There are no signs. Who must the driver of the truck give way to?
questions.explain: There are no signs, but you are driving on asphalt, and the green car is coming out of a dirt road. A paved road has priority over a dirt road ⟦119⟧, so the green car gives way to you, even though you are on its left ⟦120⟧. The blue car is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: There are no signs. In what order will the blue car, the tractor and the white car go through the intersection?
options: The tractor and the white car at the same time, then the blue car
Blue, then the tractor and the white car at the same time
questions.explain: Here, the “straight-through” road is a dirt road, and the joining road is paved. Without signs, a paved road counts as the main road ⟦121⟧, so the blue car goes first, even though it is turning left. The tractor and the white car, on the dirt road, give way to it ⟦122⟧, and their paths do not cross each other.

questions.q: The blue car is making a U-turn. Who must you give way to when turning right?
questions.explain: You are on the minor road and give way to vehicles from the main road entering your lane, including a vehicle making a U-turn ⟦123⟧. After its U-turn, the blue car will end up in the lane you are turning into, and the green car is already travelling straight along it. Give way to both: first the green car, then the blue car.

questions.q: Sign 2.3.1 is placed before the intersection. Who do you give way to when turning left?
questions.explain: Sign 2.3.1 “Crossroads with a minor road” means that you are on the main road. The motorcycle, at sign 2.4, gives way to you even though it is on the right ⟦124⟧. The oncoming bus is also on the main road, and when turning left you give way to it ⟦125⟧.

questions.q: In what order will the blue car, the truck and the green car go through the intersection?
questions.explain: The main road changes direction (plate 7.13): the blue car and the truck are on the main road, and the green car is on the minor road. Between themselves, the blue car and the truck follow the rules for a road of equal status: for the truck, the blue car is approaching from the right, so the truck gives way ⟦126⟧. The green car gives way to both ⟦127⟧.

questions.q: Who must you give way to?
questions.explain: The main road turns right (plate 7.13), and you keep going straight ahead. The green car is also on the main road, and between yourselves you follow the rules for a road of equal status: it is on your right, so you give way to it ⟦128⟧. The motorcycle, on the minor road, is turning right and does not cross your path.

questions.q: Who must the driver of the green car give way to?
questions.explain: You and the blue car are on the main road, which changes direction here (plate 7.13). Between yourselves you follow the rules for a road of equal status: you are on the blue car's right, so it gives way to you ⟦129⟧. The motorcycle, on the minor road, is entering your lane and must give way to you ⟦130⟧.
